content.text: Clear task. Spec below; please check the three assumptions.

spec.title: Monthly attendance exceptions
spec.summary: List missing clock-ins, employees late three or more times, and rows where the clock-out is before the clock-in, from the monthly time-clock export.

inputs.description: Time-clock export: one row per employee and day; '-' = missing punch.
Employees with name, team and shift start time.

steps: Read the clock events and the roster and join them on Employee ID.
Parse clock-in, clock-out and shift start times (HH:MM).
Find rows with a clock-out but no clock-in.
Find rows where the clock-out is earlier than the clock-in.
Count late arrivals per employee, excluding those error rows.
business_rules: Late = clock-in more than 5 minutes after the shift start.
Repeated Late lists employees with 3 or more late days in the month.
Late Dates is a comma-separated list of ISO dates in date order.
Rows with clock-out before clock-in are data errors and are not counted as late.
edge_cases: '-' in Clock In or Clock Out means the punch is missing.
Days without any row are absences and are ignored.
A missing clock-in is not counted as late.

schedule.notes: First working day of the next month.

assumptions: Shift Start in the roster applies to every working day of the month.
Exactly 5 minutes after shift start is still on time.
A row with a missing clock-out but a valid clock-in is not an exception.

input.notes: Times are converted to minutes after midnight for all comparisons.

content.text: The crash comes from the '-' placeholder for missing punches. I now parse with errors='coerce' so those become missing values, which is exactly what the missing clock-in rule needs.

input.notes: Unparseable times (the '-' placeholder) are now treated as missing.
